summary: Add a platform-neutral development-memory gate plus required Windows and Ubuntu CI test lanes, and add a dedicated POSIX regression proving runtime disposal kills a Python child process in the kernel process group.

pointers: POSIX Issue#72: disposing one kernel kills its descendant process group

steps: Reviewed Issue #72 and the existing Windows-only workflow. Froze the contract that both Windows and Ubuntu must gate merges and neither lane may be continue-on-error.

Separated the append-only development-memory validation into one Ubuntu job, then made test a fail-fast=false matrix over windows-latest and ubuntu-latest with identical install/typecheck/build/full-test steps.

Added a POSIX-only real-process regression: a Python RLM cell starts a sleeping descendant interpreter, runtime.dispose() kills the kernel process group, and the test polls kill(pid,0) until the descendant is gone. The test is skipped only on win32 and is included in the full test script.

evidence.target: current main CI workflow and Issue #72 acceptance contract
evidence.note: Confirmed main had one windows-latest job and a PowerShell-only memory range check; the Candidate removes the Windows-only gate structure.
Candidate is prepared for PR CI; the connected execution environment cannot run the repository locally because outbound github.com DNS is unavailable.

limitations: GitHub Actions has not executed this Candidate yet; CI result must be read back before merge.
The new POSIX regression proves descendant cleanup under the bare runtime process-group path; sandbox-runner-specific descendant semantics remain covered by their own M9 tests/contracts.

summary: First Windows+Ubuntu gate executed. Memory and Windows were green; Ubuntu exposed an existing cross-platform test-injection bug in the M3 post-read pathname identity race. The production identity check was preserved. The test now freezes canonical realpath before monkeypatching os.lstat so the second injected lstat is deterministically the post-read identity check on POSIX and Windows. The POSIX descendant regression is CI-owned rather than added to package.json, reducing unrelated package conflicts.

pointers: POSIX Issue#72: disposing one kernel kills its descendant process group
M3 Issue#24: a post-read pathname identity change is rejected before publication

steps: Read GitHub Actions run 34007391061: development-memory PASS, Windows typecheck/build/full tests PASS, Ubuntu typecheck/build PASS, full tests had exactly one failure in the M3 post-read pathname identity-change injection.

Diagnosed the failure as test-only platform behavior: POSIX os.path.realpath itself calls os.lstat, consuming the monkeypatch call counter before _read_context reaches its own post-read lstat. Production fstat/lstat identity checks were not weakened.

Applied an exact-match guarded patch through a branch-only one-shot GitHub Actions workflow because tests/rlm-loop.test.ts is 194KB and the connector only replaces whole files. The workflow deleted itself in the same commit; the final PR contains no self-modifying workflow.
Reverted the temporary package.json test-list edit and moved the dedicated POSIX descendant probe to an explicit Linux-only CI step after the normal full suite.

evidence.note: Install, typecheck, build and full test suite all passed.

One test failed: M3 post-read pathname identity-change injection; all preceding typecheck/build and the dedicated POSIX descendant cleanup regression passed. Root cause was POSIX realpath consuming monkeypatched lstat calls.
Patched only the guarded M3 test block and deleted the temporary workflow from the branch.

limitations: A new user-authored PR CI run is required after this correction because GitHub marked the bot-authored follow-up workflow run action_required without starting jobs.
The dedicated POSIX process-tree test covers the bare runtime process-group path; sandbox-runner-specific cleanup stays under M9 coverage.
